Chapter 8: Adapting the Practices to Different People and Situations
You know, no two teams—or even two people—are exactly the same. Great managers get this. They realize the five core practices we’ve talked about aren’t a one-size-fits-all formula. Instead, it’s about personalizing your approach, while still keeping things consistent and fair for everyone.
So, how do you actually tailor these practices? Let’s break it down.
First, think about listening styles. Some folks open up best in one-on-one conversations, where it’s just the two of you talking things out. Others might feel more comfortable with written check-ins, or even sharing in a group. The key? Adjust the format to match what helps each person feel at ease.
Next, feedback preferences matter a lot. Some teammates light up when they’re recognized in front of others. But for others, a quiet, specific compliment means much more. Take the time to figure out what motivates each person, and give feedback in a way that fits them.
When it comes to growth, not everyone’s looking for the same kind of challenge. One person might be eager to lead a big project, while someone else is more interested in learning new skills through training. Offer a mix of opportunities, so each person gets the kind of growth that excites them.
And don’t forget about cultural sensitivity. Our backgrounds shape how we see trust, feedback, and ownership. What works for one group might not land the same way with another. For example, a global project manager I know noticed her European team appreciated direct feedback, but her colleagues in Asia preferred a more subtle approach. By tuning in and respecting those differences, she built stronger relationships and avoided a lot of misunderstandings.
So, what’s the secret? Stay curious. Ask your team what works best for them. Be willing to adjust, even if it means stepping outside your comfort zone.
When you adapt the five core practices to the real people around you, everyone feels seen, respected, and supported—and that’s how you build a team that truly thrives.
